chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kindi, from more than one person, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who dies and has no one present to wash him except women. May women wash him? He said: “His wife or a woman within his unmarriageable kin may wash him, and the women should pour water over him from above the clothes.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Upon this distinction that we have explained, everything that has been reported concerning the general permissibility of a man washing his wife and a woman washing her husband should be understood. Among that is what he narrated:

key_terms.الثِّيَابِ: the clothes, indicating the pouring is done over garments
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the water used for the ritual washing
key_terms.امْرَأَتُهُ: his wife, who is permitted here to perform the washing
key_terms.ذَاتُ مَحْرَمِهِ: a woman who is his mahram, permanently unmarriageable to him
key_terms.زَوْجَهَا: her husband, mentioned in the juristic clarification
key_terms.غُسْلِ: ritual washing, here referring to washing the deceased
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُهُ: to wash him ritually for the deceased's ghusl

ai.seo_question: Can a wife or female mahram perform ghusl for a deceased man if no men are available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning ghusl of the deceased when no male washer is available for a deceased man. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits his wife or a woman who is his mahram to wash him, while other women may pour water over him above the clothing. The closing note explains that broader reports about spouses washing one another are to be understood in light of this legal detail.
